question.leadin: As much as 70% of the male population of this country may have been killed in the disastrous War of the Triple Alliance.
question.text: Name this country which was led by Francisco Solano Lopez from 1862 until he was killed in action in 1870.
question.clue: The most vilified leader of this country was a paramour of Eliza Lynch who shouted "I die with my nation!" at the Battle of Cero Cora.

swap.leadin: This man was the first president of Gran Colombia, and he won the battles of Boyaca and Carabobo.
swap.text: Name this South American leader known as "The Liberator."
swap.answerHtml: Simón Bolívar [or Simón José Antonio de la Santísima Trinidad Bolívar Palacios Ponte y Blanco]
swap.clue: This winning commander at Carabobo joined with Antonio Jose de Sucre to win a victory at Ayacucho.

question.text: The Dirty War was fought in this South American country, where thousands of people were killed in andaround Buenos Aires.
question.clue: Juan Carlos Ongania established a military government in this country, whose transitional replacement, Hector Campora, fell from power after snipers fired on gathered crowds at an airport in the Ezeiza Massacre.

swap.leadin: In 1948, the assassination of Jorge Eli´ecer Gait´an set off riots and started a decade-long civil war.
swap.text: Name this South American country where the ensuing riots ravaged the capital city and earned the name El Bogotazo [bo-gah-TAH-zo].
swap.clue: Gaitan's assassination in 1948 is regarded as the start of "La Violencia", a still-existing war in this country between liberals and conservatives.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the American colour-coded War Plans.
question.text: The volatile political situation in this country forced America to consider an invasion, codenamed War Plan Green. After this country's revolution ended, the political situation stabilised enough that War Plan Green never had to be put into effect.
question.clue: In order to protect refugees in this country, the LNDLR was founded and the encyclical Firmissimam Constantium was issued.
question.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

swap.text: Napoleon was willing to sell the Louisiana territory because of this conflict, which ended his ambitions of a North American empire and lost him his claims on Hispaniola.
swap.clue: The aftermath of this conflict resulted a bloody civil war known as the War of the Knives, in which one side was led by Andre Rigaud.

question.text: Following the war, the U.S. also acquired this territory, which was granted limited self-governance by the Foraker Act. Separatists from this place tried to assassinate Harry Truman in 1950.
question.clue: Revolutionaries from this place uttered the "Grito de Lares" and used the Blair House to stage an unsuccessful assassination attempt on Harry Truman.

swap.text: This war between Chile, Peru, and Bolivia was fought over a resource-rich section of the Atacama Desert, but is more commonly referred to by ocean it was largely fought in. Bolivia has been landlocked ever since.
swap.clue: The Cochrane and the Blanco Encalada were one side's main vessels, while the other side lost its main ship, the Huascar, after the Battle of Punta Angamos.

question.text: Dessalines was a lieutenant of this first major leader of the revolution. After defeating Andre Rigaud in the War of the Knives, this man promulgated an 1801 Constitution that declared Haiti a French colony and declared himself Governor-General for Life.
question.answerHtml: Toussaint L'Ouverture [or François-Dominique Toussaint L'Ouverture,or Toussaint Bréda; prompt on Toussaint]
question.clue: This man is quoted as saying "In overthrowing me, you have cut down only the tree trunk of liberty" upon his arrest in 1802 by Jean-Baptiste Brunet.

swap.leadin: This city was nicknamed the "Sodom of the New World" during the Golden Age of Piracy.
swap.text: Name this Jamaican city that was a haven for pirates until order was restored by Lieutenant Governor Henry Morgan. It fell from prominence after being devastated by a 1692 earthquake.
swap.clue: Some of this city fell into the sea during a 1692 earthquake.

question.text: Earlier in Jamaican history, these peoples' "first war" under Cudjoe was a rebellion against governor Edward Trelawney. This name was given to people who escaped slavery and formed namesake communities.
question.clue: Edward Trelawny ordered many of these people to be deported to Nova Scotia.

swap.leadin: The guerilla war stage of this conflict was ended after one leader was killed at the Battle of Cerro Cora.
swap.text: Name this 19th century South American conflict between Paraguay and a namesake coalition.
swap.clue: Bartolome Mitre was selected to lead one side of this conflict, and another commander in this war failed in his attempt to kill General Jose Antonio Correia da Camara.

question.leadin: This man agreed to go to jail in exchange for building the prison, which was nicknamed "the Cathedral."
question.text: Name this leader of the Medellin drug cartel, a notorious cocaine runner.
question.clue: This man agreed to a period of nominal captivity at La Catedral prison in exchange for a deal preventing his extradition to the U.S.

swap.leadin: Henry Kissinger decided against telling U.S. diplomats in the countries of this political campaign to warn their respective countries' leaders against terrorist acts.
swap.text: Name this political terror campaign of the 1970s in which right-wing dictatorships suppressed "Marxist subversion" in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia, and Brazil.
swap.clue: A man involved in this campaign was accused of genocide against the Ache people, and another man involved in this campaign .

question.text: July saw this brief war in Central America, which arose from anti-immigrant laws pushed for by the United Fruit Company.
question.clue: This war that began after Honduras lost 3-2 in a playoff match during the 1970 FIFA World Cup qualifier.

swap.leadin: Hilda Gadea wrote about the leadup to this event in her memoir My Life with Che.
swap.text: Following this event, Gadea learned that Che Guevara had moved on from her to Aleida March, while Che had helped create Radio Rebelde to aid the 26th of July movement in this struggle and led his forces to victory at Santa Clara.
swap.answerHtml: Cuban Revolution [DON’T READ THIS OUT LOUD but accept answers about overthrowing Batista or Castro coming to power]
swap.clue: The build up to this conflict was depicted in a Mikhail Kalatozov film, which depicted guerilla fighters in the Sierra Maestra region.

question.text: Many Latin American Jesuits identified "men for others" with the preferential option for the poor, a doctrine espoused by this founder of liberation theology in On the Side of the Poor and We Drink from the Wells.
question.clue: James Cone's work on black liberation theology predates this Peruvian priest's book A Theology of Liberation, which articulated the "preferential option for the poor" and launched the liberation theology movement in Latin America.

swap.text: This poet and musician, who had written Allende's campaign song "Venceremos" with Ittura, was among the first to be tortured and murdered at Chile's Estadio Nacional by the Pinochet regime.

question.leadin: A general from this modern country legendarily shouted "about face!" ordering his retreating men to turn and charge the pursuing Spanish calvary at the Battle of Las Queseras del Medio.
question.text: Identify this country home to that mythologically nicknamed general, who led both this country's independence from Spain and La Cosiata, the movement which separated it from a larger post-colonial state.
question.answerHtml: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela [or República Bolivariana de Venezuela] (José Antonio Páez was nicknamed the “Centaur of the Plains.”)
question.clue: An economic boom caused by oil in this founding member of OPEC lasted until the 1980's.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the short-lived First Spanish Republic.
swap.text: The brief time of the Republic also had the Spanish government continue fighting the Ten Years' War in Cuba, which more or less started when planter Carlos Manuel de Cespedes began a revolt in October 1868, an event given this name and marked by a namesake Cuban holiday.
swap.answerHtml: Grito de Yara [accept Cry of the Yara or obvious synonyms for “cry”]
